title.narrative: Land Registration and Property Valuation Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Land Registration and Property Valuation Project for Moldova is to improve the quality and transparency of the land administration and property valuation systems.The project consists of four components. 1) First Property Registration will support the first registration of public and private land in Moldova and strengthen the data quality for records already in the land register. This component will also organize mandatory public displays and public awareness campaigns to ensure citizens are engaged and aware of the procedures, activities and benefits during first property registration.Additionally, a comprehensive Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) will be set up at Cadastru to monitor feedback received from beneficiaries and provide a formal avenue to appeal. The component consists of three subcomponents: (i) systematic registration of private land—including implementation of public displays, public awareness campaigns and a grievance mechanism; (ii) systematic registration of public land; and (iii) improvement of the quality and reliability of the cadastre data; 2) Property valuation will support extending mass valuation to incorporate those properties not currently included and to carry out selected revaluation of properties to help improve the transparency of the property market and keep the property valuation system current and usable through inter alia: (i) initial valuation of properties; (ii) revaluation of properties which have not been revalued since 2008; and (iii) setting up of a property valuation infrastructure and an independent appeals system to challenge valuations; 3) Land administration system strengthening will support the strengthening of the land sector in Moldova by facilitating policy dialogue and conducting a review of the existing institutional and regulatory frameworks, proposing improvement where possible. It will also encourage a development of simplified business processes and modernization of cadastre services through use of ICT and support the development of NSDI. The component will support: (i) development of land sector and land sector sustainability polices covering governance, organizational systems, the roles of different process participants, notaries and private sector and registration and valuation processes and including, if applicable, the preparation of legal or regulatory reforms; (ii) strengthening information and communications technology capacities; and (iii) strengthening of the National Spatial Data Infrastructure (NSDI) including preparation of a business plan, expansion of the geoportal and capacity building activities for agencies responsible for the provision of core reference datasets on data standards, maintenance of metadata and creation of interoperable datasets.4) Capacity building and project management will support capacity building at stakeholder agencies and institutions to ensure the smooth implementation of project activities and support project sustainability, as well as provide support for project implementation through inter alia: (i) training and capacity building and equipping for LPA's staff as needed to support the systematic registration and valuation at the local level; (ii) training and capacity building activities at PSA's Cadastru to improve their client orientation and servicing skills; (iii) design and implementation of a comprehensive social assessment (including a social management plan) and three customer satisfaction surveys; (iv) monitoring and evaluation (M&E) of the Project; and (v) operation of Project Implementation Unit (PIU).
To improve the quality and transparency of the land administration and property valuation systems.

title.narrative: Percentage of rural residential properties valued for the first time

comment.narrative: The valuation model for rural residential properties has been developed and approved. First valuation has been conducted for 45% of rural residential properties. Property assessments however have not been rolled out.

title.narrative: Number of datasets in compliance with INSPIRE standards

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. Four (4) datasets harmonized: roads, soil, hydro and landcover.

Number of public land parcels delineated

comment.narrative: There are additional 18,000 land parcels approved by the delineation committee currently undergoing registration in cadastre.

title.narrative: Number of private land parcels registered

comment.narrative: International valuation standards adopted as national standards. The guidelines for the implementation of standards (4 sets of guidelines) have being developed with the project's support and are now with the Agency for Geodesy, Cartography and Cadastre for approval.

title.narrative: Cadastru ICT system to report gender-disaggregated property ownership data for policy and decision making
Percentage of urban residential and commercial properties revalued

comment.narrative: New values were to be produced for 5 types of urban residential and 2 types of commercial properties. For all urban residential properties new values have been calculated but not yet rolled out. As for commercial properties the models are still being developed. There could be new values calculated only for simple commercial properties by the end of the project while the complex ones will remain to be calculated during 2026.

title.narrative: Percentage of customers satisfied with Cadastru services

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. The final survey ongoing. Results and the report to be available early 2026.

title.narrative: Percentage of land in Moldova recorded in cadastre (private/public)
Information on property values and property valuation methodologies easily and widely accessible

comment.narrative: Information on property values is provided to each property owner and thus is available. Valuation methodologies are available offline but they also need to be updated. Newly develop methodologies have undergone public consultations. Decisions on models adopted are published in the "LEGIS.MD" (regulatory database). Those are: (1) urban (3) apartments, ground-floor apartments, and single family houses; (2) rural (2) houses and agriculture land. New property values should be published (thus become widely available) by end 2025.

title.narrative: Land administration system information easily and widely accessible

comment.narrative: Target achieved. The information is available at cadastre offices and through the PSA website. The number and types of information are limited, but as new information is produced, for example information from surveying works are displayed locally (offline) and through the cadastre website (online). The customers of cadastre services who access the information online assess the availability of information with an average 8.5 rating on the 1 to 10 scale.
